feat(simulator)!: the Simulator screen loses the window state, and the budget takes its place (UC-ROC-117)

The client half of the window strip-out. The server side landed in 7e1bec8.

THE STATE SET, which is what a reviewer should check first. `PublishCapability` was
`open | closed | unknown` and is now `available | unknown`; the strip's resting
`data-publish-state` vocabulary was `closed`/`open-ready`/`open-not-reserved` and is now
`unknown`/`available-ready`/`available-not-reserved`. `closed` only ever meant "no publish
window is open" and the window is deleted. "open" is renamed rather than kept, because it
described a window that had been deliberately opened and would shut itself — reusing the
word would carry the deleted mechanism's meaning into a screen that no longer has it.

AC-102-20 RE-MEASURED IN THE REAL BROWSER, not inferred. All three resting states measure
**58px** at all four gate viewports (1366x560, 1280x600, 1024x640, 1920x920), spread **0**,
and the cap case reads **58 of 80** at the 1366 floor. The parity rule is untouched; the
LIST it ranges over now asserts COMPLETENESS against `stripState`'s own resting branches, so
a state added tomorrow is measured tomorrow instead of sitting quietly outside the check.
The cap case FOLLOWS the longest resting content, which moved from `closed` (its full reason
sentence) to `unknown` (whose detail comes from the failure and so is not under our control).

THE THIRD STATE FOR A FAILED READ IS KEPT, deliberately and per the item. `unknown` is
untouched; the presenter is still STRICT (a body missing any of the four facts is `unknown`,
not a partial answer); a body still carrying `open: false` from an older host mid-rollout is
read for its facts and cannot resurrect a closed state; and the BUDGET keeps its own
`{status:"unknown"}`.

THE BUDGET IS PROMOTED, and two of its operator-facing sentences were FALSE before this.
`budgetText` said "published this window" — the capability window — while showing a figure
about the 15-minute bucket DEF-ROC-123 re-keyed it to; it now names the period. The
`capability-budget-exhausted` refusal said "This window's publish budget is exhausted" and
"A new window starts with a fresh budget; this one cannot be topped up", i.e. it told an
operator to open a window to reset a clock-based counter. It now reads the route's `scope`
and gives per-cap next actions — AC-123-5's requirement, asserted CLIENT-side for the first
time, because "the 15-minute bucket rolls over shortly" and "the daily cap resets at
midnight UTC" differ by hours.

DELETED: `remainingText` (nothing closes), the `sim-publish-remaining` span, the
`capability-disabled` refusal branch (a stale 403 now falls through to the UNRECOGNISED
branch, which is honest and transient rather than a dead end pointing at a control
DEF-ROC-123 already removed), and the arming-era comment blocks in `SimulatorPage.tsx`.

TESTS — repointed, not weakened, and each deletion states where its property went:
`screenGate.browser.test.tsx` loses the `simulator-publish-closed` entry (its `noClaims`
justification was "these facts are NOT DISCLOSED AT ALL while the window is closed"; both
halves are gone) and renames the other two; the AC-102-7 "announced in EVERY state"
enumeration loses `closed` — the state its original defect was FOUND in — and now ranges
over the two that remain; the AC-102-25 TOCTOU case follows the hazard from "the window
closed between the read and the click" to "another instance spent the last budget slot";
the AC-111-5 detail-over-error PRECEDENCE case moves from the 403 to the 503, which still
carries both fields.

`probe-uc102-live.mjs` is repointed and now asserts the ACCESS GATE from a FRESH anonymous
context — every path 401/302 except `/health` and `/api/health` at 200, including the write
route with a never-reserved node so it cannot publish — plus that the screen carries no
arming control and no arming-era copy. It exits 2 with a diagnosis rather than failing
misleadingly when the run has no session, and so does the e2e spec's `landOnSimulator`.

Green: dashboard unit 1264, BROWSER TIER 311 (the tier a red web-app job would SKIP the
deploy over, DEF-ROC-087/146), lint clean, `make typecheck` PASS on all four manifests.

head.message:
fix(uc117): close AC-117-1's three residues, and the blind spot that hid them

The tester rejected AC-117-1 on three residues. All three are fixed, and the
second one is the interesting one.

1. DELETED src/dashboard/tests/e2e/def-roc-123-armed-publish-live.spec.ts. It
   still gated on ROC_SIM_ARMED (window arming, forbidden by name) and still
   polled the DELETED strip states `open-not-reserved` / `open-ready` - the
   vocabulary is now `available-*`. It could only ever FAIL the first time anyone
   ran it, and read green solely because it self-skips and is wired to no make
   target and no workflow. Deleted rather than repaired: it tests a mechanism that
   no longer exists.

2. THE GUARD HAD THE BLIND SPOT THAT LET IT THROUGH, and this is the part worth
   keeping. uc117WindowMechanismGone.test.ts swept only src/app's src, local and
   tests - nothing under src/dashboard - while the window had a UI half. So a
   guard reporting CLEAN was measuring a tree the residue was not in. Widened to
   sweep src/dashboard/{src,tests} and to include .tsx (the residue was a .ts, but
   the strip lives in .tsx). Its test titles said "under src/, local/ or tests/"
   and now say what it actually sweeps - a title that overstates scope is the same
   fault one level up.

   Widening it immediately surfaced two more sites, BOTH legitimate, and both now
   carry the marker the guard itself prescribes:
   - publishCapability.test.ts proves a STALE 403 capability-disabled arriving
     mid-rollout from an older Function App degrades honestly rather than reviving
     the deleted copy;
   - def-roc-123-one-action-publish-live.spec.ts POSTs to the deleted arming route
     to prove it is NOT REGISTERED on the deployed host - which is STRONGER than
     this whole sweep, because a token scan sees the repo and that sees what is
     actually running.

   The narrowness pin ("exactly ONE file uses the exemption") is updated to an
   EXACT THREE-FILE LIST with a one-line justification each, so a fourth user
   still fails. Not relaxed to a count, and not deleted: its intent - stop the
   marker becoming an escape hatch - is right and is preserved.

3. class-deps.mmd:3179 - the simCapForHost label still described the capability
   route reading resolvePublishWindow PER REQUEST and "the CLOSED path (the
   shipped default)". All false of the deployed code, and it is the model a tester
   plans from. Corrected; the lazy-composition point it also makes is true and
   kept.

Green: app 2584, dashboard unit 1264, dashboard BROWSER 311, typecheck 4/4,
check-docs PASS.

fix(uc117): the change-impact model is swept mechanically, and it was false in seven places (UC-ROC-117)

Closes the last of AC-117-1's three residues. The other two were already closed by
5cc917a: the stale `def-roc-123-armed-publish-live.spec.ts` is deleted, and the guard's
sweep already reaches `src/dashboard/{src,tests}` and `.tsx`. Verified at HEAD, not
assumed.

The third was NOT closed. 5cc917a corrected the one label the tester opened by hand
(`simCapForHost`) with a minimal edit, and a minimal edit is what left the rest: run a
guard over the publish neighbourhood and the model was still false in SEVEN places
across FOUR nodes.

  simPublishHttp    an empty body "reaches the seam so the capability WINDOW is the
                    first thing any caller meets" — that gate is deleted
  simPublishForHost "The WINDOW is resolved PER REQUEST and never memoised" — it is
                    resolved not at all; it can no longer throw for an over-long one;
                    and it emits no simpublish.window composition line
  simCapHttp        "x-roc-build echoed in BOTH window states" — there is one state
  simCapForHost     "The WINDOW comes from the destination and bounds only … a warm
                    instance cannot keep reporting OPEN after the operator closed it"

Three of the four carried no `UC-117` clause at all, so they read as descriptions of
the running system. The fourth is the shape a minimal repair actually produces, and it
is why the guard has two rules rather than one: an appended "(UC-117 deleted the
window)" satisfies "does it record the removal" while the label still OPENS with a
false statement of fact. A reader meets a label front to back, so everything before the
`UC-117` marker is read as present tense and must carry no window vocabulary.

WHY A GUARD RATHER THAN A FOURTH CORRECTION. The tester found one of seven by reading.
Nothing mechanical could find the others, because this file's sweep covered TypeScript
only while the model is what a tester PLANS FROM — a false label is a false test plan,
not a documentation nicety. Now it is swept, in the same file and by the same
comment-vs-code split, so the model is allowed to EXPLAIN the removal (a rule that
forbade that would be satisfied by deleting the explanation) and a non-vacuity pin keeps
the token checks honest.

FOUR CASES, NOT THIRTEEN, and the four attach to `product/variations/UC-ROC-117.json`.
Each case loops over the seven-node vocabulary and names every offender rather than
being parameterised into one case per node: DEF-ROC-152 measured 23 of its 28 duplicates
as exactly that shape, and a seven-node loop here would have been the twenty-fourth. The
node identity is DATA; what varies across the four nodes is the KIND of falsehood the
model can carry. The variation file is PARTIAL by design and says so — AC-117-1's model
limb only, which is the limb the tester rejected on.

Green: uc117WindowMechanismGone 31/31 (was 27). App tier 2603 passed. Variation limb:
0 unknown node refs, 0 duplicates, 0 gaps, and casesWithNoVariation unmoved at its 3895
floor. §17d unmoved at 1136.

head.message:
feat(rules): an operator can RETIRE a rule -- it stops being evaluated, and stays explicable (UC-ROC-120)

THE DECISION, argued rather than assumed: RETIRE, NOT DELETE.

A decision record carries `firingRuleId: "R-<id>"` and nothing else about the
rule, so the version rows are the ONLY thing that can ever explain a ticket that
was raised -- or a fault that was silently suppressed -- months later. Deleting
them makes that permanently unanswerable for every decision the rule ever made,
and it lands on somebody who was not in the room. The store is insert-only BY
CONSTRUCTION behind a Query/Get + Insert least-privilege pin, so a delete would
also have meant widening a live IAM grant on the table that decides whether real
faults raise tickets. And the asymmetry settles it: a retirement is reversible
through the EXISTING restore route, a delete is not.

So a retirement is an ordinary appended version row carrying `retired: true` and
a snapshot with `enabled: false`. The second half is the fail-safe: selectWinner
has skipped disabled rules since UC-ROC-004, so a reader that has never heard of
retirement stops evaluating it anyway (v124 -- a control that needs every reader
to know about it is a control some reader omits).

TWO CALLS, ONE ROUTE. A body with no impactHash returns 409 plus the effect the
removal would have on the site's OWN recent decisions -- computed with the same
computeDraftTestDelta the mandatory draft-test uses, hence the same engine the
live pipeline uses -- and MINTS the confirmation keyed on it. A body carrying
that hash is recomputed server-side, requires a FRESH marker, and retires.

The gate is a server-minted marker and not a dialog, because a dialog is client
state the server cannot see. It is stricter than publish in two places (the admin
role; a refusal to touch a LOCKED rule, since retiring the global fallback is the
one click that makes a site silent) and deliberately looser in one, argued: no
recent data does NOT refuse it, because refusing would make a rule created in
error on a site with no telemetry PERMANENT -- MSP's exact condition, and the
exact defect this use-case ends.

The impact names stopsAlertingCount SEPARATELY, because removing an ALERT rule
can hand its traffic to a lower-priority SUPPRESS rule and make a real fault go
quiet, and no operator holds a site's whole priority ladder in their head.

ConfigWriteDeps.ruleRetire is REQUIRED, not optional: it broke three existing
deps bags at `tsc`, which is the property.

2704 app tests green (15 new, every one attached to a variation node), lint
clean, typecheck pass. class-deps.mmd carries the new nodes, edges and
:::uc120changed marks in this same commit.
